item.title: Lions pay tribute to injured linebacker Jack Campbell a week after he was carted off field
item.description: Jack Campbell was stretchered off the field after a brutal tackle in Week 8.
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions are letting linebacker Jack Campbell know he is in their thoughts. A week after Campbell was carted off the field and hospitalized, multiple members of the Lions showed up for Sunday’s game wearing his jersey.

The team shared a few images prior to their Week 9 game against the Miami Dolphins.

For 4️⃣6️⃣ pic.twitter.com/43xSI718tJ

— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 8, 2026

Campbell was stretchered off the field after making a tackle during the team’s Week 8 game against the Minnesota Vikings. It was clear immediately Campbell had sustained a significant injury on the play, as his arms went limp and he lay motionless on the field. Eventually, the entire Lions team came out and knelt around Campbell. Some members of the team were emotional. He was later ruled out with a neck injury.

The linebacker was taken to a local hospital and was said to be making positive progress early in the week. On Wednesday, he released a statement of his own, saying he had movement in his lower body and was “continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body.”

Campbell, who is in his fourth year with the team, was off to a strong start after making the All-Pro team last season. Through seven games, he had 57 combined tackles prior to the injury.

It’s unclear when Campbell will return to the team. While he’s out, however, Campbell will remain on the minds of his teammates. The Lions made sure to send that message Sunday.

item.title: Bengals vs. Falcons score, live updates: Joe Burrow's MVP push meets Michael Penix Jr. in Madrid
item.description: Follow along as the Bengals and Falcons face off in Madrid to kick off the Sunday slate in Week 9.
item.content:encoded:
The Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will be featured in the NFL's second-ever regular-season matchup in Madrid, with kickoff set for 9:30 a.m. ET at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium.

The Bengals (5-2) find themselves in second place in the AFC North as quarterback Joe Burrow continues to play at an MVP level. After the Tennessee Titans nearly upset them in overtime in Week 8, however, the Bengals have plenty to clean up. Burrow threw five touchdown passes but added three picks to the mix, all three of which went to safety Amani Hooker.

The Falcons are sitting on the wrong side of .500 at 3-5, coming off a disastrous performance from Michael Penix Jr. He threw a career-high four interceptions, completing just 33.3% of pass attempts for 125 yards and no touchdowns in a 16-0 shutout loss against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 8. Atlanta might not find as much relief as it would like to against the Bengals in Week 9, either; Cincinnati's defense has been productive in the turnover department this year, forcing a turnover on 14.7% of opposing drives, fifth-best in the NFL.

item.title: Cowboys vs. Colts live updates, inactives, where to watch: Jonathan Taylor, Daniel Jones play amid NFL trade dreadline rumors
item.description: Follow along as the Cowboys and Colts battle it out in Week 9 ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
Coming off a tough Week 8 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, the Dallas Cowboys might get exactly what they need by facing an Indianapolis Colts team that appears to be in teardown mode.

After trading DeForest Buckner and listening to offers for running back Jonathan Taylor,the Colts are sticking with Daniel Jones at quarterback, for now. In eight starts. Jones has completed 60% of his passes for 1.542 yards, 5 touchdowns and 9 interceptions. Jones may find some success against a Dallas pass defense that currently ranks as the sixth-worst in the NFL in total yards allowed.

But Indianapolis might benefit from handing off to Taylor against the NFL's worst rush defense, unless the preference is to save him for a possible deal. Cowboys running back Javonte Williams may also be poised for a big game versus a Colts rush defense ranked fourth-worst in the league.

At the very least, these two defenses could give up a lot of points and make for an entertaining shootout. Despite the Cowboys' record, Dak Prescott is one of the NFL's top passers so far this season.

item.title: Browns vs. Saints live updates, inactives, where to watch: Shedeur Sanders gets first start of 2026 as Deshaun Watson ruled out with concussion
item.description: Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders will make his first start of the season in Week 9 after Deshaun Watson was ruled out with a concussion.
item.content:encoded:
The Cleveland Browns go into Week 9 with a surprising 5-3 record that has them just outside the AFC wild-card playoff picture. So any and every win will be important from here on out.

However, Sunday's game will draw even more attention with Browns head coach Todd Monken announcing that Shedeur Sanders will start at quarterback while Deshaun Watson remains in concussion protocol.

While this will be Sanders' first start of the season, the second-year pro started seven games as a rookie, finishing with a 3-4 record, completing 57% of his passes for 1,400 yards with 7 touchdowns and 10 interceptions.

The Saints have lost four of their past five games, though they suffered one-score defeats in their previous two games before a bye week. QB Tyler Shough is playing well, throwing for 1,721 yards, 13 TDs and 7 INTs on a 67% completion rate. However, New Orleans ranks near the bottom half of NFC teams in total defense, allowing 372.7 yards per game.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Browns and Saints face off in Week 9, airing on CBS.

item.content:encoded:
Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season is officially the week of the backup quarterback. Days after Baltimore Ravens third-stringer Joe Fagnano was pushed into action on "Thursday Night Football," a number of backups will take the field Sunday hoping for better results.

The most notable name on that list is Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders, who will draw the start against the New Orleans Saints after Deshaun Watson was concussed in Week 8. It will mark Sanders' first start of the season.

He's far from the only backup being thrust into the spotlight Sunday. Joe Milton III will get his first start with the Philadelphia Eagles. He'll take on J.J. McCarthy, who will look to keep impressing with the New York Giants.

Elsewhere, Drew Lock will start for the Seattle Seahawks in place of Sam Darnold. He'll take on Gardner Minshew, who replaced Jacoby Brissett as the Arizona Cardinals' starter. And on Monday night, Carson Wentz will start for the Minnesota Vikings with Kyler Murray sidelined.

Additionally, there are a number of major injuries to follow heading into the week. Giants running back Cam Skattebo is doubtful with a hamstring issue. Buccaneers wideout Emeka Egbuka is in danger of missing Sunday night's game against the Chicago Bears due to a foot issue.

Also of note, we've got two teams on bye this week: the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Tennessee Titans.

item.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' RB Blueprint for Week 9
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks lays out the blueprint at the running back position for Week 9.
item.content:encoded:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be this RB column, a WR column and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available.

1. Jahmyr Gibbs (at MIA) - 133.5 proj. total yards

Gibbs survived the Vikings matchup with a top-5 finish in Week 8. Things will get easier from there. A lot easier. Across the season, Gibbs is averaging 25.5 half PPR points (RB1) on 23.7 expected points (RB1). He's leading in carries per game and second in receptions per game. What a season.

Miami ranks ninth-worst in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields (22.5 per game) and sits second in receiving points allowed to RBs. Detroit carries an implied team total of 28.75 points (third) as 7-point road favorites. This is obviously a smash spot, duh.

2. Kenneth Walker III (vs. NYJ) - 113.5 proj. total yards

Walker has had slower games against the Seahawks and healthy Broncos defenses, both clearly top-5 units to me right now. It hasn't helped that LT Josh Simmons (back/other) and LG Kingsley Suamataia (benched) haven't been active, forcing the Chiefs to dial up a ton of their runs to the right side only. Still, Walker is the RB6 on RB3 usage this month and RB2 in both metrics across the entire season. The offense at least getting Rashee Rice back in the mix will help them move the ball more often.

The Jets placed star DT T'Vondre Sweat on IR and first-round rookie DE David Bailey has missed time recently, too. They bottled up Mike Washington Jr. and the Raiders' disaster-class OL last week, but they're a unit to attack right now. Kansas City carries an implied total of 28 points (fourth) as 9.5-point home favorites.

3. Christian McCaffrey (vs. LV) - 107.5 proj. total yards

Update: Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) aren't available. Neither is Brandon Aiyuk if you were wondering.

McCaffrey is the RB6 in half PPR points per game on RB6 usage across his last four games. They needed more receiving work from CMC during this stretch with Deebo Samuel Sr. and Mike Evans missing time, and we'll see if they return off the bye. He's better without them but has been a mid-range RB1 with the WRs healthy.

The Raiders rank fifth in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields (23.4 per game) and sit third in rushing points allowed to RBs, recently surrendering an RB6 finish to Braelon Allen. San Francisco enters with a slate-high 30.5-point implied team total (first) as 9.5-point home favorites. It's a great spot.

4. Bijan Robinson (vs. CIN) - 122.5 proj. total yards

Update: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) went to IR, and they called up Khalil Herbert.

Robinson is the RB30 on RB23 usage this month. I can promise that'll be the worst stretch of his season.

The primary driver of the falloff is the on/off splits with Michael Penix Jr. as a receiver. His targets with Penix this year are 3.2 per game. His career average for context is 5.1. Part of this is Penix's inability to move, which is required to buy time in the screen game or to work to the checkdown. The ball is flying out of his hand early in the snap, and those are less likely to go to RBs. Hopefully they carve out more looks moving forward. It'd be enough of a difference to view him in the mid-range RB1 tier, instead of the elite RB1 tier.

The Bengals are much improved against the run with superstar DT Dexter Lawrence shutting down everything up the middle, but the rest of the defense is looking suspect, especially if CB1 DJ Turner (ankle) can't go. The LB and S groups are missing huge tackles weekly, and Robinson is a great candidate to rip wide zone explosives away from Lawrence in the A gap. This is what Tony Pollard did last week when he was the RB3 overall. The Falcons carry a 24.25-point implied team total (12th) as 3-point home underdogs.

5. D'Andre Swift (vs. TB) - 88.5 proj. total yards

Update: Kyle Monangai (turf toe) is unlikely to play. The splits with Kyle Monangai are staggering. We'll see if he can get cleared this week. If not, Swift has enjoyed a month-long stretch of being the RB3 on RB2 usage overall.

Tampa Bay has once again been stout against backfields this season, ranking 31st in half PPR points allowed to RBs (14.5 per game). The Buccaneers have been especially tough on the ground, sitting 31st in rushing points allowed per game to the position. Just ask Bijan Robinson (RB28), Jaylen Warren (RB23) and Javonte Williams (RB19) this month. Chicago enters as 5.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 26.5 points (seventh).

6. Javonte Williams (at IND) - 83.5 proj. total yards

Williams' lack of explosives is starting to cause the Cowboys' games, like last week in the second half when they leaned on the run game and it went nowhere. For fantasy purposes, it largely hasn't mattered because of his red-zone role in this top-10 offense. He's the RB12 on RB4 usage this season, despite being the RB11 in carries and RB23 in receptions.

His fantasy RB1 value is completely tied to scoring touchdowns. Since joining the Cowboys, he's averaged 16.5 points when they've scored 30+ points versus 15.1 in the 20s and 9.4 in the teens.

The good news is the Cowboys project for 28.75 points (second) against a Colts defense that looks lifeless without DT DeForest Buckner. Bhayshul Tuten just finished as the RB2 without playing the fourth quarter, and Chris Rodriguez Jr. was trucking defenders himself. Indianapolis has allowed the sixth-most rushing yards per game this season, and that will probably only get worse.

7. Rhamondre Stevenson (vs. GB) - 86.5 proj. total yards

Update: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was ruled out again. I hope he is alright. There is a history brewing here, and he's so young. Here's more on that:

In light of TreVeyon Henderson sharing he had a medical emergency and "unexplained neurological symptoms," here's what he told @TyDunne last year about having sleep paralysis: https://t.co/f4H4BZuDRT

Thankfully, Henderson said, tests have "come back positive and reassuring." https://t.co/GbG4oYahTGpic.twitter.com/iSJcvMLsMS

— Andrew Callahan (@_AndrewCallahan) November 6, 2026

There are notable splits for Stevenson whether he plays or not. In seven games dating back to last year where Hendo missed or had fewer than five carries, Stevenson is the RB13 on RB16 usage. He drops to RB25 on RB39 usage in the other 19 games. This year, Stevenson is the RB20 on RB28 usage while he's been in and out of the mix. It helps if A.J. Brown and Hunter Henry join Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins on the sideline, too.

Green Bay represents a favorable rushing matchup, ranking seventh in half PPR points allowed to RBs at 23.1 per game. The Packers sit sixth in points allowed to RB rushing at 16.6 per game, having yielded top-24 fantasy finishes to Chuba Hubbard (RB7), Jahmyr Gibbs (RB18), Javonte Williams (RB17) and D'Andre Swift (RB12) in four consecutive weeks. New England hosts the Packers as 3-point home favorites with an implied team total of 25.25 points (10th).

Underrated Week 9 injuries on defense:
+ DEN: Panthers w/o DE1, LB2, fill-in CB2
+ Rhamondre: Packers w/o LB1, LB2
+ NYJ: Chiefs w/o CB1, CB2, DT2
+ KC: Jets w/o DT1, DE2
+ MIA: Lions w/o DE2, CB1, LB1
+ LAR: Commanders w/o DT1, DT2
+ IND: Cowboys w/o DE2, maybe LB1, CB1

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 8, 2026

8. James Cook III (at MIN) - 97.5 proj. total yards

Truly nothing has changed. Cook is the RB4 on RB9 usage this season, averaging 101 rushing YPG (third) on RB41 receptions per game. The Bills offense looked particularly great last week with DJ Moore stretching the field and Dalton Kincaid ripping explosives in multiple TE sets.

The challenge here is the Vikings defense. They just held the Lions to 19 points on the road and are clearly one of the only truly elite defenses. Detroit leaned on the ground game a bit more than usual against them, a trend that's appeared throughout the season against Minnesota. It's allowed the No. 16 rushing YPG versus the No. 31 passing YPG. Opposing offenses have a 45% neutral pass rate against them (second lowest). That said, Jahmyr Gibbs (RB5) and Jonathan Taylor (RB8) both held the line, while mediocre schemes/players have completely busted. Buffalo heads to Minnesota as 3.5-point road favorites with a 25-point implied team total (11th).

9. Bucky Irving (at CHI) - 83.5 proj. total yards

The Bucs are coming off the craziest two-game run script I can remember. Irving has been the RB4 and RB11, respectively in expected half PPR points in them, while Kenny Gainwell has popped off alongside him. Tampa Bay is content running the ball behind its fantastic OL, and while it won't be anywhere near this extreme, I don't see that game plan changing after Baker Mayfield struggled in a pass-first offense early on. Irving's vision and contact balance are a great fit to consistently hit these 20-yard runs. This month, Irving is the RB2 on RB3 usage. He handled the goal-line carry last week, while Sean Tucker looked on from the sideline.

The Bears defense has been stingy against opposing backfields, ranking 29th in half PPR points allowed to running backs at 16.7 per game. Then they added the best DT in Jeffery Simmons. This will be a tough test for an on-fire Bucs run game. The Bears held Bijan Robinson to an RB31 finish in Week 6 and bottled up both Seahawks RBs last week. Tampa Bay heads on the road as 5.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 21 points (22nd).

10. Kyren Williams (at WAS) - 86.5 proj. total yards

Williams' role is nearly the same, but the Rams offense hasn't been quite as explosive recently, so his output has slightly turned down. This month, he's the RB17 on RB16 usage, averaging 14.5 carries and 3.0 receptions. He was catching more passes early on, and it's possible the increased usage of 13-personnel is working against his passing role. Blake Corum continues to play every other drive; Corum is an NFL starter on tape to me.

Washington sits 27th in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields at 17.0 per game on the season, but DT Daron Payne just went to IR. The top-end RBs have played well, including Christian McCaffrey (RB2) and Jonathan Taylor (RB9). Even Saquon Barkley (RB21 in a part-time role) looked good last week. The Rams travel as 5.5-point road favorites, carrying an implied team total of 26.5 points (eighth).

11. Jonathan Taylor (vs. DAL) - 85.5 proj. total yards

Taylor had his worst game since Week 8 of 2024. That did come against the best fantasy RB defense (Jaguars), but it did also come without LG Quenton Nelson during the middle of Taylor's own trade talks. The Colts been mixing in Seth McGowen earlier in games more than they did before, and their defense is getting blown out, which means Taylor can get scripted out of games. It's nowhere near the same situation as before, dropping him to boom-bust RB2 levels. I anticipate him being far more matchup-elastic given his poor surroundings.

Luckily, the Cowboys are a great spot. They've allowed the third-most fantasy points to RBs on the most rushing yards per game (152.8). It was Tyler Allgeier's turn last week (RB1 overall), but Saquon Barkley looked good on his limited touches the week prior and Bucky Irving dropped 175 yards in Week 5, too. It's bad versus bad on this side of the ball. The Colts have a 22.75-point team total here. It's a much better spot than last week, pending reports that Taylor's role could be changed the week before the trade deadline.

12. Chuba Hubbard (vs. DEN) - 90.5 proj. total yards

Update: Star LG Damien Lewis (knee) is out. It's a bad game to miss with menace DT Zach Allen on deck.

Hubbard has been a high-volume anchor, sitting as the RB9 in per-game half PPR points on RB6 usage across his last four contests despite some difficult matchups. He's handled 19.3 carries per game (RB7) over that window, crossing the 20-carry threshold in three of those four outings. In Week 8 against Green Bay, Hubbard set season highs with eight targets and seven receptions, turning that receiving work into 21.4 half PPR points on 24.1 expected points. Jonathon Brooks is starting to practice, but they'll ramp him up slowly and he's unlikely to factor in too much when he is cleared.

The Broncos defense ranks 11th in half PPR points allowed to RBs at 21.9 per game on the season, but their starting lineup is finally back to normal. Opponents have had success through the air against Denver, where the defense allows 8.5 half PPR points per game to receiving RBs (fourth-most in the NFL), highlighted by Emmett Johnson's RB5 finish in Week 8. Carolina's offense also brings distinctive passing tendencies, holding a 62% neutral pass rate that ranks third-highest in the league. The Panthers enter the matchup as 3-point home underdogs with an implied team total of 20.25 points (25th).

13. Josh Jacobs (at NE) - 69.5 proj. total yards

Jacobs was the RB1 overall in usage last week after being the RB5 in expected half PPR points in his debut. He's averaging 18.9 half PPR points on 23.4 expected, essentially trading a couple of runs for a couple of targets in this more pass-heavy Packers offense. That's a great trade-off in fantasy. For context, the Packers had a 46% neutral pass rate in 2024-25 versus a 56% rate this year.

On tape, Jacobs is not in his prime, nor is the Packers offensive line, so he'll definitely be an inefficient player. Green Bay can't trust MarShawn Lloyd in protection or to hit the right hole, so they'll live with whatever Jacobs can produce.

The Patriots rank 26th in half PPR points allowed to opposing running backs, giving up just 17.0 points per game to the position. This was true the year prior, so it's a matchup worth knocking expectations. Recent bell cows D'Andre Swift (RB13) and Braelon Allen (RB19) were just fine. Green Bay heads on the road as 3-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 22.25 points (17th).

14. Chase Brown (at ATL) - 75.5 proj. total yards

Brown was the RB20 on RB14 usage last week despite finishing with eight receptions. The good news is Brown still has 8-catch grabs in his pocket and those eventually will lead to more explosives and touchdowns. The problem was he played 2 of 8 snaps inside the 10-yard line, including 1 of 4 inside the 5-yard line. That's where Samaje Perine is mixing in more than normal. Across the month, Brown is the dang RB39 on RB11 usage. He'll settle in as a fantasy RB2 with upside, but the pass game is too good and Brown is too mid to believe in a full top-10 RB1 rebound here.

The matchup with the Falcons is a solid one. They've allowed the sixth-most points to fantasy RBs and were just embarrassed by Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell last week. Atlanta has allowed a top-10 fantasy RB in 4 straight outings, and EDGE Samson Ebukam just went to IR. They've missed a LB, too. The Bengals project for 27.75 points (fifth).

15. Bhayshul Tuten (at BAL)

Tuten is a game-time decision with an ankle/foot injury. He hasn't practiced yet but his last play in Week 8 was a touchdown that didn't look painful. This is a good reminder that Chris Rodriguez Jr. is one of the top insurance options in fantasy.

Tuten sits as the RB10 in per-game half PPR scoring on RB18 usage over his last four contests. He has generated efficient production on the ground and through the air, averaging 72 rushing yards (RB13) and 36.3 receiving yards per game (RB7) across that window. Coming off a bye in Week 8, Tuten set season highs with 28.9 half PPR points (RB2) and 104 rushing yards against Indianapolis. The potential for a low-end RB1 finish following that Week 7 bye is pretty clear.

The Ravens present a difficult matchup, ranking 23rd in half PPR points allowed to running backs at 17.3 per game. Baltimore is particularly stout against pass-catching backs, ranking 29th by allowing just 3.7 half PPR receiving points per game. That matches its recent stretch, having limited Chase Brown (RB36) and Bijan Robinson (RB18) to modest days in Weeks 7 and 5, respectively. The Jaguars enter Thursday night as 8.5-point road favorites with an implied total of 25.5 points (ninth).

16. Jonah Coleman (at CAR) - 83.5 proj. total yards

With RJ Harvey (knee) on IR, the backfield was down to two. JK Dobbins started, but just like last week, it was Coleman who ended it. Dobbins was held to just one (one) snap in the second half of Week 8, while Coleman was left wide open for a 51-yard reception and ultimately cut back on a separate carry for a score. He finished as the RB11 on RB6 usage, tallying 11 carries and four receptions. He handled goal-line carries on separate drives, too.

Coleman has a little windup step when buying time as a runner, and he can find some cutback lanes that others won't see. He is a low-built power runner who will try to lower his shoulder for an extra yard. At the same time, he's probably the slowest fantasy starter and did bounce some runs to play into his weakness. He looks like a Day 3 talent who is climbing the depth chart by having fresh legs with some established trust. It's unlikely that Dobbins ever threatens on passing downs, so Coleman is at least the passing-down back with an emerging rushing role. We'll see if the Broncos actually trade for Jonathan Taylor later on. For now, Coleman is an RB2/3.

The upcoming matchup brings a Carolina defense allowing 26.1 half PPR points per game to running backs (second most). The Panthers have been particularly vulnerable on the ground, ranking second in rushing fantasy points allowed to opposing backfields. Recent opposing rushers have capitalized, including Bucky Irving (RB2) and Josh Jacobs (RB10). Denver heads in as 3-point road favorites with an implied team total of 23.25 points (13th).

17. Woody Marks (at LAC) - 78.5 proj. total yards

It sounds like David Montgomery is going to miss another one. In three games without him, Marks is the RB29 on RB17 usage, 16.3 carries and 2.7 targets per game. Marks is a replacement-level back who can play in all phases, but expecting efficient outings behind this OL is asking too much. He's finished below his expected half PPR point totals in 5 of 7 games.

The good news is the Chargers' run defense isn't one to fear. They rank 10th in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields at 22.2 per game. Los Angeles has been particularly vulnerable against ground games, ranking fourth in rushing points allowed per game to running backs (17.3) while ranking 27th against RB receiving. It's allowed a top-16 finish in 4 straight games, including Blake Corum (RB15), Kenneth Walker (RB1), J.K. Dobbins (RB16), and Emanuel Wilson (RB6). Houston enters the contest as 4.5-point road favorites with a 22.5-point implied team total (16th).

18. Ollie Gordon II (vs. DET) - 78.5 proj. total yards

Gordon has taken on significant rushing volume, ranking as the RB16 in half PPR points per game on RB12 usage across his last four outings. Over that stretch, he is averaging 17.8 carries (10th) and 90 rushing yards (eighth), while logging nine carries inside the 5-yard line. His passing-game involvement remains minimal, however, so the risk of being scripted out of the game plan is concerning against great opponents.

The matchup is tough against a Lions defense allowing just 16.2 half PPR points per game to RBs (30th most). Detroit ranks 25th in rushing points allowed and 24th in receiving points allowed to opposing backfields. Miami operates with a run-heavy approach, ranking 30th in neutral pass rate at 44%, while Detroit opponents pass at an extreme 59% clip (third highest). The Dolphins enter as 7-point home underdogs with an implied total of 21.75 points (18th).

Lions LB Jack Campbell will not be out there. It was relieving to hear that he has movement in his lower extremities.

19. Devin Singletary (at PHI) - 75.5 proj. total yards

Update: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is doubtful. Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring) is on IR. Najee Harris isn't coming back. It's Singletary and backup RBs I've never heard of. He's been with the team for awhile and is fairly trusted, even if he doesn't offer much beyond what is in front of him. That's okay in fantasy football. We're here for the touches. For reference, the Giants' RB room has averaged 19.5 expected half PPR points, and Singletary is probably looking at 75% of that here. We're approaching "Too Big To Fail" territory.

The Eagles' run defense hasn't lived up to their potential. Their DTs are hot and cold in a lost season, and their EDGEs aren't as good as they've been in previous DC Vic Fangio defenses. The Giants have a solid 20.75-point team total (21st) despite being on the road. They are field goal favorites, though Singletary is pretty game script proof.

20. Derrick Henry (vs. JAX) - 80.5 proj. total yards

Henry has played seven games without Lamar Jackson over the last three years, and he's averaging 16.8 half PPR points on 17.5 expected points and 22 carries per game. That's the absolute upside case, but the reality is his new baseline is far lower with Tyler Huntley also out and with OC Declan Doyle finding more ways to move the ball than running behind an aging Henry. The last month of the year are a great example of that, when he's been the RB28 on RB17 usage and 17.3 carries per game. That's a better baseline with "Joe Fagnano" under center on Thursday Night Football.

Jacksonville has been the most difficult fantasy RB matchup this year, allowing just 14.2 half PPR points per game to the position on the fewest rushing YPG (77.4). Opposing offenses have the lowest neutral run rate against them, too. It'll be a little easier without DT DaVon Hamilton, but this remains a matchup to avoid. The Ravens only have a 14.75-point team total as 10-point dogs. Henry can get game-scripted out of outings, just as Jonathan Taylor (RB37 on RB20) usage was last week.

21. Ashton Jeanty (at SF) - 64.5 proj. total yards

Jeanty is the first player to have the same or fewer carries in 8 straight games to open a season, per Doug Clawson on X. I don't think this was pre-game comments or ankle-related either. Coach Klint Kubiak has been scaling down his carries for a long time and communicated to Jeanty before this game of the role change.

"Who is playing the best ball at the time" https://t.co/wuA7cZ2Z2f

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 2, 2026

Week 8 easily could be a one-game experiment to fix a completely broken run game, but it'd be a surprise if Jeanty went back to his early-season workhorse role. It's clear Kubiak, who pounded the table for Mike Washington Jr. and wasn't around for the Jeanty top-10 selection, views this duo as closer to even than Twitter does. Some of that is scheme-related, as Washington is a better athlete for the wide zone, while Jeanty's power-based skill set is struggling to find cutback lanes and hit the hole in time.

Jeanty's pass-game role is very safe, and I'm currently projecting a more even split on early-down runs, just how it has been from Week 3 on when he's been the RB18 on RB15 usage. The error bars here are obviously extremely wide, but if there's a game script that leans Jeanty, it's clearly while trailing. The Raiders are 10-point dogs to the 49ers.

22. Quinshon Judkins (at NO) - 81.5 proj. total yards

Judkins' role is changing for the worse with Dylan Sampson back in the mix. His expected half PPR points have dropped from 13.8 to 11.4 since his return and all of that has come from the receiving game, where his targets' split is 4.0 to 1.5. If the Browns start trailing, Judkins is now at risk of a total dud. He's been the RB22 and RB26 in usage over the last two outings and has been fairly inefficient throughout the year, making him a FLEX rather than a fantasy RB2.

The Saints represent a prime rushing matchup, ranking first in half PPR points allowed to running backs at 27.9 per game. New Orleans has been especially vulnerable on the ground, allowing a league-high 21.2 points per game to RB rushing (first of 32). Over their last four games, the Saints have yielded spike performances to Bijan Robinson (RB5), Brian Robinson (RB8), Aaron Jones (RB7) and Tyrone Tracy (RB8). Cleveland travels as 2.5-point road underdogs with an implied total of 20.5 points (24th).

23. Saquon Barkley (vs. NYG) - 68.5 proj. total yards

Update: Barkley was only able to muster up a limited practice this week in practice, a sign that his lingering injuries haven't fully healed.

Barkley scored in the red zone on a Wildcat run, showcasing enough speed to get to the pylon. He generally looked just fine on tape, but the Eagles had to bring down his workload again. He's been the RB32 and RB22 in usage over the past two games, and in Week 8, he played just one snap on late downs and 44% of snaps on early downs. It'll be hard to reach top-15 status until he's unbothered by his back and hamstring.

A date with the Giants is neutral, revenge game aside. They're mediocre against the run in general, but both teams can play a run-heavy, slow-paced style that limits fantasy points in general. The Eagles only have an 18.0-point team total; we'll see if anything changes with QB Joe Milton starting over Tanner McKee.

24. Alvin Kamara (vs. CLE) - 63.5 proj. total yards

Update: Travis Etienne (hamstring) is due back in the next two weeks but not yet. The Saints fired their OL coach during the bye week, then released Kendre Miller on Saturday. On top of that, CJ Donaldson (shoulder) was ruled out. Miller and Donaldson have taken a third of the workload each without Etienne. He'll compete with Audric Estime this week, and Estime is really limited to downhill rushing. It's the best Kamara has looked all year. He's been the RB24 on RB43 usage this past month and was up to RB23 usage in Week 7. He's a great FLEX play.

Cleveland ranks 17th in half PPR points allowed per game to opposing running backs (19.3). The Browns have been far more vulnerable to ground attacks than pass-catching backs, ranking 9th in rushing points allowed per game to backfields but 30th against RB receiving (3.5 points per game). Cleveland has given up big games on the ground over recent weeks, including 143 rushing yards and an RB9 finish to Jaylen Warren in Week 8 and an RB1 overall finish to Tony Pollard in Week 7. New Orleans is listed as 2.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 23.0 points (14th).

25. Jadarian Price (vs. ARI) - 69.5 proj. total yards

The backfield is set. Emanuel Wilson was active but didn't play and is on track to be a healthy scratch moving forward, leaving Zach Charbonnet, Jadarian Price and George Holani as the active players. Charbonnet started and played 37% of snaps, leading to 11.6 expected half PPR points (RB22 usage). Price played 48% of snaps, leading to 9.9 expected half PPR points (RB30). Holani played 17%. The trio played on both early and late downs, pass-protected, ran routes and carried the ball.

It's officially a "let-the-best-man-win" committee, for an organization that held back Kenneth Walker III for years. So who looked the best? Take a look at this:

comparing the seahawks RBs on similar looks pic.twitter.com/Z4LWcLbtKV

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 3, 2026

Athletically, it's no contest. Price is so much faster in a straight line and laterally agile. The speed difference is evident on the outside runs, while the lateral ability is easier to see on the cutback runs. That's not the end-all, be all, but it absolutely does matter and it's unlikely to change with Charbonnet coming off a February ACL surgery. Price was the one to receive the pitch on a sweep, so the coaching staff obviously agrees.

That said, Price did have two reps where he probably could've done a lot more with the look. One of them featured him not giving his center the time to climb to the next level. He instead jammed into a crowded lane, where a more patient and crafty runner would've cut back for a nice gain. The other rep was attempting to bounce it outside of nickel CB Kyler Gordon, when he could've hit his inside shoulder hard for a potential nice gain. Neither was egregious, but the top-end veterans treat them differently.

Charbonnet's runs were more textbook, but there was space to carve out real explosives if he was simply faster. Both of the runs in the video above showcase that glaring flaw. I'd understand they always value Charbonnet's size and quality decision-making in short yardage, but the Seahawks would do well if they continued giving Price a lot of the early-down and between-the-20s runs to increase their odds of an explosive and to give Price more time on task to develop.

Arizona ranks 18th in half PPR points allowed to opposing running backs, yielding 19.3 fantasy points per game to the position. The Cardinals sit 19th against RB rushing and 18th against RB receiving, having recently surrendered big finishes like Jahmyr Gibbs (RB1) in Week 5. Seattle enters as 11.5-point home favorites with a 28-point team total (fifth). They didn't have DT Walter Nolen last week and EDGE Josh Sweat is on the trade block.

26. Blake Corum (at WAS) - 59.5 proj. total yards

Corum is very good, as is the rushing scheme and blocking. It's also helping that Matthew Stafford's elbow is bothering him, which has led the offense into very long drives. Corum can't keep up this RB12 on RB40 usage pace from the past month, but he has been the RB26 on average this season. He's getting every other drive and projects better in positive game scripts. The Rams are 4.5-point road favorites here with the No. 7 team total (26.0).

27. Rachaad White (vs. LAR) - 57.5 proj. total yards

Jeremy McNichols (foot) is going to miss months, leaving White and Austin Ekeler at the top of the pecking order with Devin Neal and Craig Reynolds available from the practice squad. White and Ekeler are battling it out in all phases, with White starting last week and finishing off the win with an explosive and goal-line TD late in the fourth quarter. White was the RB17 on RB17 usage last week and was the RB11 on RB22 usage before that. His fantasy low-end RB2 case is pretty straightforward.

The Rams rank 27th in half PPR points allowed per game to opposing backfields (17.0). Their DL is strong enough to overcome a scheme that is daring teams to run. Offenses facing Los Angeles have posted a 47% neutral pass rate, which is the third-lowest rate in the league. Because the Rams are light in the box and teams are often trailing, they have allowed the seventh-most receiving points to RBs, which plays into White's game. Ashton Jeanty was a PPR scam in Week 7 (RB10), and Bam Knight (RB20) and James Cook III (RB4) got home in the weeks before that. Washington is listed as a 5.5-point home underdog with an implied team total of 21.0 points (23rd).

28. Breece Hall (at KC) - 66.5 proj. total yards

Update: Hall was able to rack up back-to-back full practices this week and will play. We'll see how the split looks, but Hall is unlikely to return to his RB12, RB13 and RB33 finishes to start the year with Braelon Allen playing so well in his absence. That's particularly true with the Chiefs on deck. They've allowed the 25th-most rushing yards per game (96.3). If forced to guess, Hall starts the game and is the primary pass-catching back, while Allen mixes in fairly even in terms of carries. It's possible Allen even steals goal-line looks after plenty of between-tackles success so far. A two-back committee with a 19.5-point team total is that of a zero-floor FLEX. It doesn't help that the Jets have been linked in trade talks with Hall.

29. Tyler Allgeier (at SEA) - 70.5 proj. total yards

With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) picking up his third separate high ankle sprain of the season, Allgeier has a chance to consolidate most of the Cardinals' touches. We'll see if Bam Knight (concussion) can get cleared in time. Without him, Allgeier is looking like one of the biggest workhorses of the week. The Cardinals' RB room collectively has averaged 21.5 expected half PPR points per game this year, and if he inherits 80% of that, then he's a top-24 option.

That will be stress-tested against the Seahawks, however. Gardner Minshew will make his first start against a top-2 defense. They've only allowed 94.0 YPG on the ground this year, and they recently kept Kenneth Walker III to 57 and Christian McCaffrey to 83 total yards. D'Andre Swift's 3-score outing on Monday Night Football is absolutely the exception, and the Cardinals unit is nowhere near the Bears'. Arizona has a highly concerning 14.5-point team total.

What can go wrong?

30. Chris Rodriguez (at BAL)

31. Zach Charbonnet (vs. ARI) - 56.5 proj. total yards

See Jadarian Price.

32. Jordan Mason (vs. BUF) - 52.5 proj. total yards

33. Aaron Jones Sr. (vs. BUF) - 44.5 proj. total yards

The Vikings backfield is so split down the middle that it's rendering both backs next to useless, at least until they figure out how to score more points. Minnesota is 31st in RB usage this season, averaging just 17.4 expected half PPR points to the entire backfield. If this hovers around a 50/50 split, then Jones and Jordan Mason are in the 7-10 points range on average. Last week, it was even worse because game script went away from them. Jones was the RB43 in usage (5.3 expected points), while Mason was the RB47.

Game script isn't expected to be better this week against the Bills. The Vikings are 3-point dogs with a team total of 20.75 points (23rd). The Bills have been pretty bad against fantasy RBs this season, but these teams also haven't had Carson Wentz at QB. To Jones' credit, the Bills rank 11th against RB rushing (14.1 points allowed per game) and 3rd against RB receiving (9.3 points allowed per game). Jones is more likely to catch passes, while Mason is more live for a goal-line plunge.

34. Braelon Allen (at KC)

With Breece Hall (quad) practicing in full and calling himself "the starter", it's officially time to scale back Allen's role. In the 3 games with him to start the year, Allen was nowhere near fantasy viable, seeing just 8 total opportunities per game.

Now, he's earned more work than that, but it'll be surprising if he catches many passes at all or clears more than 12 carries. The Jets have averaged 18.4 expected half PPR points (28th) to their RB room across the entire season, and Allen should be somewhere in the 30-50% range of it moving forward. 40% of that means 7.4 expected points, essentially a pretty tough FLEX to fantasy RB4. There's more upside with him because he may be their goal line back, but Allen is best viewed as a Brian Robinson Jr. type.

This matchup is scary as well. The Chiefs are 25th in rushing yards allowed, and New York is expected to lose by 9.5 points. That game script works in Hall's favor. Not Allen's.

35. Mike Washington Jr. (at SF) - 40.5 proj. total yards

As President of the "Mike Washington might eat into Ashton Jeanty's workload" Club, this is not the week to double down on what happened last week when Klint Kubiak experimented with very clear roles. Washington was fine behind a terrible Raiders' OL on tape, but he didn't do anything extra either. Jeanty will handle all pass down work and may even sub in at the goal line as the more powerful short-yardage back, so even if Washington is a between-the-20s ballcarrier, we have to be careful with matchups. The Raiders are 8.5-point dogs to the 49ers, who might have Nick Bosa back.

item.description: WVU loses to Texas Tech 53-48 in one of the wildest games I’ve ever seen. To be honest, it’s one of the most frustrating losses to I’ve experienced as a WVU fan as well. Let’s get into the why, and I’ll explain the frustrating part as well. Defense (or lack thereof) New game. Same story. […]
item.content:encoded:
WVU loses to Texas Tech 53-48 in one of the wildest games I’ve ever seen. To be honest, it’s one of the most frustrating losses to I’ve experienced as a WVU fan as well. Let’s get into the why, and I’ll explain the frustrating part as well.

Defense (or lack thereof)

New game. Same story. Our defense stinks. This season is starting to turn into one long “What if?” What if our defense hadn’t given up 41 points in the first half? What if we got 1 stop against Iowa State? What if we tried tackling someone against Oklahoma State?

Our defense forced 1 punt in the first. Here are the rest of the Texas Tech offensive possession’s in the first half:

  • 5 plays 65 yards Touchdown
  • 1 play 71 yards Touchdown
  • 7 plays 75 yards Touchdown
  • 8 plays 75 yards Touchdown
  • 2 plays 81 yards Touchdown
  • 6 plays 75 yards Touchdown
  • End of half

Gross.

Now it has to be said they the defense played much better in the 2nd half. They held Texas Tech scoreless in the 3rd quarter and made them work for their scores in the 4th. But that’s almost more frustrating than a silver lining at this point. What the hell happened in the first half? One or two broken coverages or missed assignments that result in a touchdown, before seeing your defense lock in and play well is one thing, but look at those scoring drives we gave up in the first half. The Texas Tech offense was playing against air.

Our pass coverage either gets flagged for pass interference or gives up a long completion, EVERY SINGLE TIME. The Texas Tech quarterback put the ball in harms way multiple times with WVU defenders in better positions to make a play on the ball than the receivers, and they all resulted in completions instead of pass breakup, or god forbid an interception for us. Texas Tech got conservative with their play calling in the 3rd quarter and we did a much better job at stopping the run, but then they remembered that we can’t defend the pass and they started scoring again. Game over.

Offense

Listen, we lost this game because of our defense full stop. We scored 48 points on the road in the Big 12. Even after giving up 41 points in the first half our offense did enough to get us a lead in the 2nd half which is pretty amazing. But…

Our offenses inability to produce points when they have the opportunity to put us up by 2 scores reared it’s ugly head again this game. Can someone just tell Rich Rod that we are down by 7 every time he is calling plays?

At the end of the 3rd quarter the WVU defense forced a punt giving the ball back to the offense with a 48-41 lead. We had all the momentum and needed to step on their throat. What did we do?

3 plays -4 yards Punt

The play calls: 1 yard run up the middle, 0 yard run up the middle, 5 yard penalty, Incompletion on 3rd and 14.

Gross.

Our defense forced a field goal on the next Texas Tech possession so the WVU offense gets the ball again in the 4th quarter now with their 2nd chance to go up 2 scores. What did we do?

3 plays 9 yards Punt

The play calls: 1 yard run up the middle, 8 yard pass, 0 yard run up the middle.

Gross.

Texas Tech would score a touchdown on their next possession taking the lead and that would be enough for them to get the win.

I know we are focusing on 2 possessions and basically asking for perfection from the offense and Rich Rod as a play caller, but this has been a trend. As great as the offense has been, they just simply refuse to go up by 2 possessions and I blame the play calling. Michael Hawkins Jr. had thrown the ball great all day when allowed to by Rich. Let him go win the game.

Once Texas Tech took the lead and put us in predictable passing situations, Michael Hawkins did not look great anymore and really struggled to get rid of the ball. To be fair though we are playing into the strength of an extremely talented defense. One that we scored on at will when we kept them guessing, but as soon as we got predictable their front dominated.

Why this one is so frustrating

This is type of win that could have set us up for a really special run to end the season. We came out of the bye week and we played a really good game one offense. We had the lead, and I would even say control of the game in the 4th quarter, and instead of a win and the momentum that comes with it, it’s a loss and we are asking the same story we have for much of the season. Are we wasting one of the best offenses in WVU?

The answer is yes. We can still make bowl eligibility and 7 wins would be good, but the opportunity for anything special to come from this season, just went out the door with that loss.

What are you thoughts on the game? Let me know in the comments!

item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions are coming off back-to-back intense NFC North rivalry games and now head south to take on the struggling Miami Dolphins. Detroit enters the game on a three-game winning streak and looks to keep it alive before heading to Germany.

Last week, my predictions went one-for-three, with the Lions’ defense holding up their end of the bargain, but the offense wasn’t as explosive. Quarterback Jared Goff couldn’t throw as much as I wanted, and wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown was limited as running back Jahmyr Gibbs took over the game in the second half.

With us back at even, it’s time to get back on the winning side on Sunday. The odds are with FanDuel Sportsbook.

1. Jahmyr Gibbs 125+ rushing yards (+220)

Speaking of Gibbs, he should continue that hot streak heading into Week 9. The Dolphins’ run defense has been rough, ranked 31st in PFF with a 51 run-defense grade and 26th in DVOA against the run. While they’re allowing only 113 rushing yards per game, this offensive line could be the best unit they’ve faced this season. How the Lions offense finished the game against the Vikings last week, where they ran it down their throats, felt like a moment when everything clicked on the offensive line.

Miami has faced top-end running back talent this season in Christian McCaffrey and Kenneth Walker III, but Gibbs has turned his game up during the winning streak. He’s averaging 140 yards per game, and that’s up against one of the best defenses in the Vikings and a solid defense in the Green Bay Packers. Facing a defense that is struggling to stop the run, I think Gibbs has another stellar performance on Sunday.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $32

2. Malik Willis under 208.5 passing yards (-113)

Back-to-back matchups against struggling offenses, I think Detroit can take care of business defensively. Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis is averaging 181 passing yards a game, and despite the Lions being without cornerback D.J. Reed, this secondary has been improving during this win streak. The Dolphins’ passing attack also lacks playmakers, which should make it easier for the Detroit defense to defend.

The Lions secondary held the Vikings with a fully healthy offense of Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson, and Kyler Murray to just 185 passing yards. Now, they face a team with Malik Washington and Greg Dulcich as their top options. No disrespect, but those players are not on the same level as the Vikings’ receiving core.

The Dolphins’ poor offensive line play will also help. Ranked 31st in pass blocking with a 53.6 PFF grade, going up against a Lions pass rush ranked third (79.9 grade) in PFF, Willis could have a long day in the pocket. He can move his legs to extend plays, but he might have to do that all game against Lions EDGE Aidan Hutchinson. I can’t see Willis having a dominant game against an improving defense that will play their hearts out for their star linebacker, Jack Campbell.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.85

3. Sam LaPorta anytime touchdown (+180)

Covering tight ends has been a problem for the Dolphins defense. Through seven games, they’ve allowed 483 yards and six touchdowns by tight ends. The Lions’ passing offense could be searching for answers if St. Brown has a limited snap count due to his injury, which opens the door for a touchdown for tight end Sam LaPorta.

LaPorta had a hot start to the season, scoring three touchdowns and getting 40+ yards per game in the first five games. The past two weeks have been a step back for LaPorta: four catches for 51 yards, with no touchdowns. Facing a team that almost averages a tight end touchdown every week, I think he finds the end zone here and has a solid performance on Sunday afternoon.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $28

If you want to turn these three single bets into a same-game parlay, the odds are +1438 and $10 -> $153.85

Record: 10-11

Brandon’s Bold Bet

If you want to go bold and build a big parlay that could pay well, put these three bets together in a parlay:

  1. Sam LaPorta over 48.5 yards (-113)
  2. Jahmyr Gibbs 2+ touchdowns (+145)
  3. Sione Vaki Alt rushing yards: 20+ (+114)

I talked earlier about the tight end struggles for the Dolphins, and LaPorta will not only find the end zone, but I think he finishes with over 50 yards. Miami is allowing an average of 69 yards against tight ends this season, so asking him to hit just under 20 yards below that seems possible. In every game where LaPorta has gotten over 50+ yards, he’s also scored, so my above prediction and this one go hand in hand.

As I mentioned earlier, the Dolphins’ run defense has been rough, and while I think Gibbs will have a good day, I see him finding the end zone not once, but twice this week. Detroit will lean on the ground game, and once they build a big enough lead, they will want to drain the clock and get the game over with. That opens the door for backup running back Sione Vaki to get more snaps and chances to rush for over 25 yards.

He’s coming off a career performance against the Vikings and is earning the Lions coaching staff’s trust and confidence to get the ball more. He will start to chip into Gibbs’ carry load a bit, but Gibbs is best when he is fresh and not overloaded, so this will help both of them achieve their goals. Playing this rough run defense again amplifies how much easier this should be for Vaki to hit. He is questionable with an ankle injury, so if you want to bet this, wait until the inactives are announced 90 minutes before kickoff.

Odds +770 and bet $10 -> $87.04

Record: 0-7

Do-it-all parlay

If you want to combine all six plays into a parlay and go big, here are the odds:

  1. Jahmyr Gibbs 125+ rushing yards
  2. Malik Willis under 208.5 passing yards
  3. Sam LaPorta anytime touchdown
  4. Sam LaPorta over 48.5 yards
  5. Jahmyr Gibbs 2+ touchdowns
  6. Sione Vaki Alt rushing yards: 20+

Odds +9168 and bet $10 -> $926.83

Record: 0-7

Use this information however you like. You can ignore it and watch the game, or, if you want to risk some money, follow these recommendations or test your own luck. Whatever you decide, please gamble responsibly and bet only money you can afford to lose.

The Miami Dolphins host the Detroit Lions on Sunday, hoping to bounce back from a Week 8 loss and pull off an upset win in Week 9. Miami enters the weekend 1-6 and in last place in the AFC East, but they hope to keep improving week to week, even if that growth doesn’t always lead to a win. The Lions are 5-2, but are third in the NFC North and need to continue to pile up wins if they want to return to the top of the division as they were in 2023 and 2024.

This game also features the return of Lions head coach Dan Campbell to Miami for the first time as a head coach. The former NFL tight end started his coaching career in 2010 as an intern with the Dolphins. He then took over as the team’s tight ends coach in 2011, holding the position through 2015. That final year, he was also named the team’s interim head coach after the team fired Joe Philbin; Miami went 5-7 in the 12 games with Campbell as their top coach.

After five years with the New Orleans Saints where he was the tight ends coach and assistant head coach, Campbell was named the Lions head coach in 2021. That year, the Lions were in complete rebuild mode. They finished 2021 3-13-1, but that has been their only losing season under Campbell, with the team averaging 11.25 wins over the past four seasons.

The 2021 Lions rebuild could serve as the model Miami follows, albeit five years later, in its current rebuild under first-year head coach Jeff Hafley.

item.title: Week 9 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Bears have momentum going into Sunday night vs. Buccaneers
item.description: The Buccaneers are coming off two straight wins, including a shutout win over Atlanta.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Bears hype is about to get very loud.

This NFL season seems wide open. There isn't one great team yet and there are few trustworthy contenders who have emerged. The Bears seemingly saw it the same way when they traded two first-round picks for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.

And through one game, it seems like a transformative trade. The Bears had a fantastic performance on a national stage, shutting down the Seahawks in a 34-17 win. Chicago's Super Bowl odds took a leap, as did Caleb Williams' MVP odds. In a season dying for a dominant team to emerge, maybe it's Chicago.

The Bears' offense isn't a question. It has scored 30 points in every game Williams has started and finished (it did score just three points against the Vikings and Williams played three-and-a-half quarters, but that says something about Minnesota's defense). If Simmons has as big of an impact on the defense as it appeared on Monday night, Chicago will be looking really good. Nobody paying attention to the NFL hadn't seen how dominant Simmons is, but it was still impressive to see how quickly he fit in and made plays.

Chicago gets another close-up in prime time this week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night. Surprisingly, the Buccaneers are far better analytically than their 3-5 record would suggest. They're fifth in DVOA, eight spots ahead of the Bears, and eight in net EPA (expected points added) per play. The Bears are strong in net EPA, coming in third.

The Buccaneers will be completely overshadowed in this game. The Bears will be the focus on Sunday night as they've emerged as one of the NFL's most dangerous teams. That's a reason they're a healthy 6.5-point favorite. That's a lot of points, and the Buccaneers might be secretly pretty good. That's why Buccaneers +6.5 is the pick. And if the Bears blow out Tampa Bay in a big prime-time window, they'll take over as the talk of the NFL, if they're not already.

Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 9 of the NFL season:

Bengals (-3) over Falcons

The Bengals and Falcons go to Madrid, Spain, for this one. The Falcons are nearly impossible to figure out. They followed up a win over the undefeated 49ers by losing to a Buccaneers team that didn't complete a pass. That sums up Atlanta's season. We should trust Joe Burrow, who is on a heater, though there are more questions about Cincinnati's defense after it gave up 36 points to the Titans at home last week.

Giants (-3) over Eagles

Maybe Joe Milton III gives Philadelphia a boost and the Eagles get their first win since Week 2. But since Jalen Hurts went on IR, the Eagles have lost all three games by double digits. It's not a good team in any way, and Milton is far from a sure thing. The Giants are off a bye and should be feeling good coming into this one.

Panthers (+2.5) over Broncos

The Broncos are the better team. A few things work against them in this spot: It's an early start on the East Coast, and the Panthers have three days rest advantage. The Broncos are also coming off an emotional win over the Chiefs and there could be a letdown. Denver has been much better at home this season. Carolina has faded after a good start but this is a decent opportunity for a win.

Dolphins (+7) over Lions

Give Miami credit for playing hard. Maybe at some point that effort starts to fade, but the last time they truly got blown out was Week 2. They lost by 14 points to the Chiefs, but Kansas City led by only seven points with three minutes left. It's possible the Lions score enough to cover, but remember that they're usually a different team outdoors.

Chiefs (-10) over Jets

Kansas City will enjoy the breather after facing the Seattle and Denver defenses on the road the past two weeks. This seems like the type of game in which the Chiefs could take out their frustrations on an opponent that does have some talent but has won only once since Week 1.

Saints (-3) over Browns

The Browns are likely going with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback because Deshaun Watson was put in concussion protocol. It's not like Watson was playing so well he's irreplaceable, but Sanders has thrown only three passes all season. The Saints are well rested coming off a bye. The Saints are not a great team this season, but this might be a spot for them to get right.

Rams (-5.5) over Commanders

Is it time to trust the Rams? They have covered two games in a row without a sweat. Those wins came against mediocre (Raiders) or bad (Chargers) teams, but they did handle business. And the Commanders are mediocre at best and maybe just bad. Let's see if the Rams are truly back.

Cowboys (-5.5) over Colts

It is incredibly hard to trust the Cowboys, especially as a road favorite. But what we saw from the Colts last week in a 42-7 loss was troubling. There was no fight left in that team, which has lost key players to trades and knows its season is done. This could be a bad mistake, trusting a defense that can't stop anyone to cover almost a touchdown on the road. Taking the Colts at this point is even harder.

Texans (-4.5) over Chargers

It's a lot for Houston to be favored by this much on the road, however, home-field advantage has been mostly eliminated this NFL season and the Chargers have no home-field advantage — even if that was still a thing. Houston is coming off a bye and still has hopes to revive its season. The Texans still have a 34.4% chance to make the playoffs according to DVOA. The Chargers are 0.0% on that list. They'll cover a spread at some point but it's hard to anticipate when it happens.

Raiders (+10) over 49ers

The Raiders have four losses, and they came against four of the better teams in the NFL: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills and Rams. The bad news is this week they get the Super Bowl favorites. The 49ers should be getting many players back after their bye. But the Raiders can move the ball and they're getting a lot of points.

Seahawks (-8.5) over Cardinals

With all the quarterback chaos this week, we get two teams that had a different quarterback in Week 8. Brissett was benched and traded, and Gardner Minshew II takes over. Sam Darnold has a quad injury and he'll be out, with Drew Lock taking over. Lock is a reasonable replacement, and Minshew isn't facing the Cowboys defense this week.

Packers (+3) over Patriots

The Patriots have a lot of injuries and the Packers have a few days of extra rest. In a game that seems evenly matched, the small edges add up. Green Bay started the season very slow but has looked much better over the last four games, winning three and barely losing at Detroit. New England has also emerged after an early-season slump to win four of five. This is a really fun matchup, and even enough to feel OK taking the points.

Vikings (+3.5) over Bills

This is an interesting game because the teams have opposite strengths. The Bills have a great offense and bad defense, and the Vikings have a bad offense and great defense. The Minnesota defense held the Bears to three points after all; Chicago has scored 30 points in every other Caleb Williams start. It will be a great test against Josh Allen, who is having another fantastic season. It's never enjoyable to be going against Allen, but getting 3.5 points with a defense this good seems right … as long as the offense does at least a little bit.

item.description: Here are a few betting trends to help you with your NFL wagers in Week 9.
item.content:encoded:
The most intriguing game on the NFL's Week 9 slate? Without question, it's the one anchoring the 15-game slate: a Monday Night Football showdown between the Bills and Vikings in Minnesota.

Not because the two teams are both 6-1 (tied with San Francisco for the best record in the league). And not because each franchise is 0-4 in Super Bowls. Rather, this interconference battle pits the NFL's highest-scoring offense (Buffalo) against the stingiest defense (Minnesota).

Flip the field, and the contrasting styles are still present: Only six teams are scoring fewer points per game than the Vikings, and only nine squads are giving up more points than the Bills.

So of course I'm capping my Week 9 NFL betting trends report with a comprehensive Bills-Vikings breakdown. That's preceded by four of the week's other top matchups, including a pair of Super Bowl rematches. 

Bengals (-3, 52.5) at Falcons (in Madrid, Spain)

Moneyline: Bengals -155/Falcons +130

• The Bengals took the field in Week 8 as the largest favorite of the NFL season to date, but never came close to covering the 13.5-point spread in a 43-36 overtime victory over visiting Tennessee.

Cincinnati has won three in a row, topping 30 points in each contest. It's the team's longest positive run since closing out 2024 on a five-game winning streak. 

However, since opening the season with back-to-back spread covers, the Bengals have gone 1-3-1 ATS. One positive NFL betting trend for Joe Burrow and Co.: They've won three of their first four road games (2-1-1 ATS). 

• Atlanta didn't allow a single completed pass last week against the Buccaneers, but still got blitzed 16-0 as a 2-point road underdog in soggy Tampa Bay.

The Falcons are 1-3 SU/ATS in their last four games. The lone victory: a Week 7 upset of previously undefeated San Francisco at home. That also stands as the team's only SU/ATS triumph in four home games.

• Atlanta is 0-2 SU/ATS against the AFC North this season, losing 20-13 at Pittsburgh as a 6.5-point underdog in Week 1 and 30-23 to Baltimore as a 3-point home favorite in Week 5.

Conversely, the Bengals have taken down the only NFC opponent they have faced (a season-opening 33-27 victory over Tampa Bay as a 3.5-point home favorite).

In fact, Cincinnati has won and covered five straight games against the NFC South dating to 2022, with each victory by at least four points.

• The over is 5-2 in Bengals games this season (3-1 on the road). What's more, each of their last nine games against an NFC South squad have topped the total.

On the other hand, Atlanta has followed a 4-0 over stretch with consecutive unders. The last time three straight Falcons games fell short of the total: Weeks 1-3 last season.  

Broncos (-2.5, 43.5) at Panthers

Moneyline: Broncos -150/Panthers +125

• Denver rallied from an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit Sunday, upending the Chiefs 28-24 as a 1-point home underdog.

Since an ugly 31-10 season-opening loss at Kansas City, the Broncos are 6-1 SU and ATS, winning and covering their last four in a row. 

Despite this hot run, Denver enters Week 9 with a scant plus-7 point differential.

• Carolina has lost back-to-back games for the first time this season, following a 43-13 Week 7 home loss to Tampa Bay with a 27-19 defeat at Green Bay on Thursday Night Football.

The Panthers have averaged 30.3 points in their three victories (tallying at least 25 in all three) and just 16.3 PPG in their last three losses (falling short of 20 points in each).

• Here's a stunning NFL betting trend that speaks to the Broncos' grit: Since Week 5 of last season, they have won 15 consecutive regular season games decided by eight points or fewer.

Although Denver is just 9-6 ATS in those 15 contests, it has covered the spread in each of its five one-score victories this season. Also, the Broncos are 5-0 SU and ATS as a favorite in 2026.

• Carolina failed to deliver for bettors against both the Buccaneers and Packers. 

It's the first time the Panthers have suffered consecutive point-spread setbacks since an 0-5 SU/ATS slump from Weeks 5-8 in 2024 — a stretch of 34 contests (one playoff game included).

Over those 34 games, Carolina is 11-3 ATS as a home underdog, with eight outright upsets (1-1 SU/ATS in that role this season).

• Broncos QB Bo Nix threw one interception in each of his team's first three contests. He has not been picked off in five games since (157 pass attempts).

This week, Nix faces a defense that has only intercepted four passes, including just one since Week 3.

Conversely, since the start of 2025, eight of the Broncos' 11 games away from the Mile High City — including three of four this year — have come up short of the total. Combined points in their four road games this year: 41, 38, 40 and 46 (over).

Packers at Patriots (-3, 46.5)

• The Packers rebounded from a last-second 20-17 Week 7 loss at Detroit as a 4.5-point underdog with last week's 27-19 Thursday night win over Carolina as a 3.5-point home favorite.

Not only has Green Bay won four of its last five, but it has followed an 0-3 ATS start to the season with a 5-0 ATS uptick. It's the team's longest stretch of profitability since going 8-0-1 ATS from Weeks 2-10 in 2021.

• New England traveled to Miami in Week 8 as a 7-point favorite but had to rally from a 10-point halftime deficit to secure a 24-19 victory. It was the Patriots' third straight non-cover after a 4-1 ATS start.

• The Packers came through for bettors in their last two road trips, covering as a favorite at Tampa Bay in Week 4 and as an underdog at Detroit in Week 7. 

Prior to that, though, Green Bay had been in a 2-10-1 ATS funk away from Lambeau Field (including a wild-card game at Chicago last year).

• New England has successfully defended its home turf this year, toppling the Steelers, Raiders and Jets by the combined score of 91-39. 

Had New York not scored a late spread-covering touchdown in a 26-19 Week 6 loss as a 7.5-point underdog, the Patriots would be on a 6-0 ATS run in Foxborough.

As it is, since Week 4 of last season (including the playoffs), New England is 11-1 SU/9-3 ATS at home and 16-1 SU/12-5 ATS as a favorite.

• During its current 4-1 SU run, Green Bay's defense is allowing just 14.6 PPG. That explains why the Packers' last five games have dipped under the total.

Since a disastrous 0-4 SU and ATS start to 2026, the Bucs have won and covered three of their last four (including two in a row). In fact, the 3-1 ATS run comes on the heels of an 0-13 ATS drought – the longest losing stretch against the number in modern NFL history.

Also worth noting: Tampa has played 31 games since its last three-game ATS winning streak. 

• Chicago traveled to Seattle on Monday night as a 3.5-point underdog and manhandled the defending Super Bowl champs, rolling 34-17.

The Bears are riding a three-game SU and ATS winning streak, and their 6-2 ATS mark is tied with Denver, Pittsburgh and Las Vegas for tops in the NFL. 

• Not only is Chicago tied for the best point spread record through eight weeks, but it has been the NFL's best bet for nearly two calendar years.

Since Week 17 of 2025 and including two playoff games last season, the Bears are on ATS runs of 21-7-1 overall, 11-4 at home and 10-5 as a favorite.

That said, there is an NFL betting trend working against Chicago this week: Favorites of six points or more are 26-11 between the lines this season but just 10-24-3 ATS.

• The Bears' last three games hurdled the total after the previous four stayed low. It's Chicago's longest streak of overs since its first five games of 2023 eclipsed the total.

Furthermore, the under is 8-2-1 in the last 11 games at Soldier Field. Only three of those featured more than 45 combined points.

The under is also 4-2 in the Bucs' last six, with only one of those contests — a 43-13 rout of Carolina in Week 7 — ending with more than 45 total points.

Bills (-3.5, 46.5) at Vikings

Moneyline: Bills -180/Vikings +150

• Only three franchises enter Week 9 with just one loss, and two of them will square off Monday night in Minnesota.

Buffalo has rebounded from its lone setback — a 29-26 upset loss to New England in Week 4 — with three straight victories (2-1 ATS). The latest was Sunday's 36-10 shellacking of banged-up Baltimore as a 3-point home favorite.

Meanwhile, the Vikings' 11-game winning streak ended in Week 8 with a 19-15 loss at Detroit as a 3.5-point underdog. Minnesota started its heater 7-0-1 ATS, but is just 1-3 ATS since.

• The Bills are unbeaten in three road games this year (2-1 ATS), and they're 5-1 SU/4-2 ATS as a favorite.

Additionally, since the 2022 season kicked off, Buffalo is 14-4 SU/13-4-1 ATS when laying fewer than four points in the regular season. That includes 11-3 SU/10-3-1 ATS as a road favorite of less than four points.

• Minnesota has covered in just four of its last 11 home games, going 1-3 SU and ATS as a home underdog.

The Vikings also have cashed only five times in their last dozen outings as an underdog, regardless of venue. The winner covered the spread in each game.

• The Vikings' 2026 opener — a 39-22 rout of Green Bay — easily topped the total. They have since stayed under in six straight games, none of which even reached 40 combined points.

In fact, in 10 games dating to Week 16 of last year, division rivals Green Bay (22) and Detroit (19) are the only teams to score more than 16 points against a Minnesota stop unit yielding a league-low 13.3 PPG.

• Buffalo is averaging 33.3 PPG, which is nearly four points more than the NFL's second-most prolific offense (Cincinnati at 29.4 PPG).

So, it's no surprise that five of Buffalo's seven games have jumped the total. Go back to last season, and the Bills are on a 9-3 over surge, including 5-0 on the road. Those five road games featured 66, 43, 68, 71 and 63 total points.

item.title: Cowboys have ideal chance to end streak of allowing 20 or more points
item.description: It's been nearly a year since the Cowboys held an opponent under 20 points.
item.content:encoded:
It's been nearly a year since the Cowboys held an opponent under 20 points. The best chance to end that streak comes later today.

At 1:00 p.m. ET, the Cowboys visit the Colts. And the Colts have scored a total of 17 points since waving the white flag with the same-day trades of guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the 49ers.

Of course, they've played a couple of very good defenses, at Minnesota and at Jacksonville. Still, with the organization creating a clear impression that they've embarked on a rebuilding plan during the 2026 season — and with trade talk hovering as to running back Jonathan Taylor, quarterback Daniel Jones, and receiver Josh Downs — the Cowboys are catching the Colts at an ideal time for Dallas.

For now, the Cowboys have allowed 20 or more points for 15 straight games. It's the longest active streak in the league, and the longest streak in franchise history.

The Cowboys last held an opponent under 20 points on November 17, 2025, in a Monday night 33-16 win over the Raiders. Since then, the Cowboys have allowed 21, 28, 44, 34, 34, 23, 34, 28, 20, 34, 30, 24, 23, 21, and 33 points. That works out to an average of 28.7 points allowed per game.

Today's the day the run could end. If it doesn't, who knows when it will?

item.title: New York Jets vs Kansas City Chiefs Pre-Blame Ball
item.description: This could be a long day for the Jets defense
item.content:encoded:
Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage for the Jets in the upcoming game. Occasionally we might hand out a pre-blame ball. If we think the Jets are going to get slaughtered, we’ll try to identify a prime culprit.

One caveat: the quarterback is off limits. Nothing personal against quarterbacks, but they are obviously the most important players on the field. We could give out a pre-game or pre-blame ball to the quarterback virtually every week, but that would be boring, so we’re not going to do it. We’ll try to identify somebody besides the quarterback for the glory or the ignominy. 

This approach comes with the obvious drawback that predictions are difficult, especially about the future. We’re destined to get many of these wrong. No matter. We’ll have some laughs along the way. Let’s get to it.

Today, for the first time this season, we’re handing out a pre-blame ball. It’s difficult to see a plausible Jets path to victory against the Chiefs in Kansas City, so pre-blame ball it is. The pre-blame ball for the Jets game against the Kansas City Chiefs goes to (drum roll please) – the interior defensive line!

The Chiefs lead the NFL in yards per rushing attempt this year at 5.1 yards per attempt. After years of struggling to run the ball, the Chiefs signed Kenneth Walker in the offseason. Problem solved. Walker is second in the NFL with 110 rushing yards per game. He’s averaging a ridiculous 5.5 yards per carry. In short, Walker and the Kansas City running game are a problem for Chiefs opponents.

The Jets have not defended the run particularly well this year. Ollie Gordon and the Miami Dolphins lit the Jets up for 150+ rushing yards two weeks ago. A week prior to that the Jets couldn’t stop Patriots third string running back Corey Kiner from running the ball right down their throats to close out a Patriots win. A few weeks before that the Chicago Bears absolutely torched the Jets on the ground to the tune of 230+ rushing yards.

All those games came BEFORE the Jets place their best run defender on the defensive line, T’Vondre Sweat, on the injured reserve list. Now Sweat is out and the Jets are facing arguably the best running game in the NFL. To make matters worse, Harrison Phillips has been battling an injury and did not practice this week until Friday. This could be a long game for the Jets’ run defense.

Ordinarily a team might try to compensate by loading the box with eight and nine man fronts. The Chiefs, however, are no ordinary opponent. They have Patrick Mahomes at quarterback. Load up the box to try to stop the run and Mahomes will surely burn you through the air. The Jets will have to pick their poison, and I’m guessing they’d rather not try to stop Mahomes with little help over the top.

This seems like a nightmare matchup for a Jets run defense that has struggled this season. The interior defensive line was already getting pushed around with Sweat in the lineup. Without him, and with a hobbled Harrison Phillips who was struggling even when healthy, look out. This could get ugly.

Jets interior defensive line, come on down! You’ve been singled out for blame before the first snap is taken. Let’s see you prove me wrong.

What about you? Who would you give the pre-game or pre-blame ball to? Let us know in the comments.
