item.title: What happened to Jack Campbell? Latest injury update on Lions LB
item.description: The Lions are getting set for their first game without Jack Campbell. Here's the latest injury update on the LB's condition.
item.content:encoded:
When the Detroit Lions take the field in Week 9 against the Miami Dolphins, they'll be doing it without a key member of their defense – Jack Campbell.

It marks the Lions' first contest since the linebacker suffered a terrifying neck injury during the team's Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings. The injury left Campbell laying on the field motionless before being carted off the field on a backboard as emotional teammates looked on.

Campbell issued a statement about his condition on Wednesday, Nov. 4. He said that he has movement in his lower body and was making progress towards regaining movement in his upper body. It was an encouraging update that extended beyond the generic ones provided earlier in the week.

EXLCUSIVE: Rare diagnosis could explain Lions LB Jack Campbell's neck injury update, spine experts say

On Nov. 7, the Lions announced they were placing the linebacker on injured reserve. It's a reminder that Campbell has a long way to go in his recovery.

As for his teammates, they are back to work without him. Here's what to know about Campbell and the latest on his condition.

What is Jack Campbell's condition?

Campbell announced in a statement on Nov. 4 that he has full movement in his lower body. He is continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body.

It was the first concrete update on Campbell's condition since the injury occurred on Sunday, Nov. 1. Prior to Campbell's statement, the team had issued more general updates, saying that preliminary results were positive.

Is Jack Campbell paralyzed?

Campbell appears to have avoided the worst fears that immediately followed his injury, as his updates indicate that he has avoided full paralysis from the neck down. Campbell said he has "full movement in my lower body" and was working to regain upper-body movement as part of his recovery.

Latest Jack Campbell injury update

Jack Campbell has been placed on injured reserve, the Lions announced on Nov. 7.

The linebacker announced in a statement on Nov. 4 that he has full movement in his lower body and is continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body.

Dan Campbell previously provided small update on Jack Campbell's status during a Tuesday, Nov. 3, radio appearance on 97.1 The Ticket.

"It's not easy because he's always going to be on our minds over here," Dan Campbell said of Jack Campbell, when addressing the Lions' preparation for Week 9. "The good news is he is improving."

The Lions coach made it clear he is providing his players with updates about Jack Campbell's status through the team's captains.

"I think the thought of him – knowing he's doing better, and I've kept the captains up to date, and they've let the other guys know its good news," Dan Campbell said, referencing how players were reacting to the situation. "I think that helps everybody just get a better handle on all this."

Campbell also added that he is trying to keep his players focused on their upcoming game against the Miami Dolphins, expressing concern that "bad things can happen" if players aren't able to be all-in on their gameday responsibilities.

REGGIE BROWN: Ex-Lions LB reflects on life-altering injury after Jack Campbell hospitalized

What happened to Jack Campbell?

Campbell went down with a neck injury after tackling Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson.

He stayed down as the training staff and medical personnel surrounded him and a cart arrived. Campbell was loaded onto a backboard before the cart took him off the field. He was transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury after exiting the team's Week 8 win over the Vikings.

The Lions announced late Sunday night that Campbell was resting and was scheduled to remain in a local hospital overnight for continued evaluation and monitoring.

JACK CAMPBELL: Lions All-Pro linebacker to remain in hospital after scary neck injury

Jack Campbell statement

Jack Campbell issued a statement, via the Lions' X account on Nov. 4. Here it is, in its entirety:

My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we’ve received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express.

I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.

My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this.

I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you.

I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done.

To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people.

One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge.

Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough.

God is good. My faith is strong.

Jack Campbell

Who is Jack Campbell?

Campbell is a linebacker for the Detroit Lions.

The 26-year-old is in his fourth NFL season, all with Detroit. The Lions drafted Campbell with the 18th overall pick in the first round of the 2023 NFL Draft after he starred in college for the Iowa Hawkeyes.

A native of Cedar Falls, Iowa, Campbell broke out during his junior season with the Hawkeyes, totaling 143 tackles, two interceptions, two fumble recoveries and a sack in 2021. Returning for his senior season, Campbell was named an All-American in 2022 and received the Butkus Award as the top linebacker in college football.

He also received the William V. Campbell Trophy, also known as the "academic Heisman," in 2022 for being recognized as the college football player with the best combination of academics, leadership and on-field performance.

More: Jack Campbell is a Lions team captain. Here's why his teammates love him

Campbell slid right in as a key piece of the Lions' defense after arriving in the NFL. However, he didn't officially break out until his third season. Campbell recorded 176 total tackles, three forced fumbles and five sacks en route to being named a first-team All-Pro and earning his first Pro Bowl appearance last season.

On May 21, 2026, the Lions recognized Campbell's breakout with a four-year, $81 million extension.

item.title: Daniel Jones, Derrick Henry lead latest NFL trade deadline rumors
item.description: Colts, Chiefs, Titans, and Jaguars are among the teams looking to make deals ahead of the NFL trade deadline
item.content:encoded:
The NFL trade deadline is closing fast, and the rumors are heating up.

Here is the latest set of rumors ahead of Sunday’s action.

The Daniel Jones trade market

Yes, you read that correctly.

There is a Daniel Jones trade market.

According to ESPN, the Indianapolis Colts have received calls from “multiple teams” regarding the veteran quarterback, who is in line to start for the Colts on Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys. Earlier this week it was reported that Indianapolis is waiting to see how Week 9 unfolds before completing any additional trades, even as the rest of the league believes the team will complete a mini “fire sale” after dealing guard Quenton Nelson and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner.

While Jonathan Taylor has received the bulk of attention, ESPN notes that the Baltimore Ravens were one team to “check in on Jones” before completing a trade with the Arizona Cardinals for Jacoby Brissett. Speculation centers on the Minnesota Vikings, who enter Week 9 with a 6-1 record, but have struggled on the offensive side of the football.

Jones signed a two-year, $88 million extension back in March.

He also has a $10.51 million injury guarantee for the 2027 season, that becomes fully guaranteed on March 15 provided he remains on the Colts’ roster. If the 2-6 Colts are eliminated from playoff contention, Indianapolis might sit him down to avoid exposing him to injury, putting a benching into play.

ESPN noted that if Jones wanted to play elsewhere, he could waive that guarantee.

And one wonders if the Colts’ decision to wait until after Sunday’s slate of games is — in part — leaving the door open for a team to develop a pressing need at the position due to an injury to a starting quarterback.

What about Josh Downs?

Jones is not the only player on the Colts receiving attention, as wide receiver Josh Downs already requested a trade following the deals involving Nelson and Buckner.

According to Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter, the Colts have informed teams that an offer of a fourth-round pick for the wide receiver has been submitted. Indianapolis initially requested a third-round pick for Downs, and you can expect the Colts to try and see if they can get a better offer for making a deal.

Jaguars looking for defensive playmakers

The Jacksonville Jaguars look like one of the NFL’s elite teams, coming off Thursday night’s blowout win over the Baltimore Ravens.

But the organization is looking to help on the defensive side of the football.

Jacksonville lost defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the rest of the season due to a torn quadriceps muscle, so adding some help along the defensive line stands out as a pressing need. And Jacksonville does have a player that could be on the block at a position of need for several teams, specifically wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. According to ESPN, the team has received “multiple inquiries on [Thomas] in recent years while resisting all overtures.”

But with Thomas seeing less and less time on offense — he played just 19 snaps against the Ravens and did not catch a pass — this might be the time to move him. One of the teams interested in his services is the Kansas City Chiefs, who have “continued to be intrigued by Thomas,” and you could see Jacksonville try and wrestle away some defensive help from the Chiefs.

Ravens not expected to deal Derrick Henry

Despite the Baltimore Ravens’ recent struggles, the team is not expected to move running back Derrick Henry in a trade before Tuesday’s deadline.

Baltimore’s four-game losing streak, and Lamar Jackson’s thumb injury, sparked the idea that the Ravens would be sellers ahead of the deadline, and opened the door to speculation about Henry’s future with the team. But the running back himself said after Thursday night’s loss to the Jaguars that he is not “going anywhere else,” and the team so far has agreed with that assessment. ESPN noted that the Ravens are not “expected to trade” Henry, and the trade for Jacoby Brissett is one sign that Baltimore is still trying to stay in the playoff fight, rather than waving the white flag on the season.

Titans “open to offers” on Calvin Ridley

While Josh Downs is one name leading the list of available wide receivers, Calvin Ridley is another AFC South WR that could be on the move.

While the Tennessee Titans are not going to trade Tony Pollard, the team is “listening” on offers for Calvin Ridley, according to ESPN, who could be acquired in exchange for a late-round pick. As noted by ESPN the Chiefs are one team calling about wide receivers, as are the San Francisco 49ers and the Pittsburgh Steelers.

However, there is some question about whether Pittsburgh is really going to trade for a WR. Earlier this week longtime Steelers writer Gary Dulac was adamant that the team was not going to move for a receiver ahead of Tuesday’s deadline.

Will that change?

Chargers not trading any of their stars

The brutal start to the season for the Los Angeles Chargers has led to open speculation about the future of several key figures, from head coach Jim Harbaugh to offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, as well as questions about several star players including Justin Herbert, Ladd McConkey, and Khalil Mack.

However, those questions have received “hard nos” from the Chargers in response.

Harbaugh addressed the Mack speculation earlier this week, telling reporters that “I want Khalil Mack here. Khalil Mack wants to be here.” And calls about both Herbert and McConkey have been rebuffed. While the Chargers have almost no chance at reaching the playoffs, the team “doesn’t like the message of giving up on the season,” according to ESPN.

item.title: Minnesota vs. UCLA: The Elite, The Meh & The Ugly
item.description: Another week, another loss to a Top 10 team
item.content:encoded:
The Minnesota Golden Gophers (5-4) were sunk by a fourth quarter to forget as their upset bid short-circuited in a 34-20 loss to the No. 8-ranked UCLA Bruins (9-0).

The Elite

The Gopher run defense. UCLA came into the game boasting the Big Ten’s top rushing attack, averaging 219.5 rushing yards per game. The defensive game plan was to stop the run and Minnesota succeeded for the most part, limiting the Bruins to 98 rushing yards through the first three quarters. UCLA was able to tack on yards on the ground in their final two possessions, once the game was out of reach and the goal was to chew up game clock. But credit to the Gopher defense for putting the brakes on a high-powered run game. Unfortunately, the plan to force the Bruins to beat them through the air backfired spectacularly.

Jalen Smith. It has not been the breakout season fans had hoped for, but the third-year wide receiver had his best game of the season, recording five receptions for 85 receiving yards. Smith sparked Minnesota’s first touchdown drive of the game with a 21-yard reception to end the first quarter, and he put the Gophers in the red zone in the fourth quarter with an impressive 35-yard back shoulder catch down the sideline.

George Rohl. With top tight ends Pierce Walsh and Julian Johnson both sidelined with injuries, the true freshman tight end is seeing the field more and hauled in his first career touchdown reception on Saturday.

Turnovers. The Bruins have won the turnover battle week in and week out all season long, but on Saturday it was Minnesota that had the edge in turnover margin. Linebacker Maverick Baranowski read the eyes of UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach perfectly in the closing minute of the second quarter and stepped in front of a pass for an interception, setting up a game-tying field goal drive before halftime. Later, rush end T.J. Bush prevented the Bruins from taking a two-touchdown lead with a strip sack in the red zone in the fourth quarter.

Quayd Hendryx. The freshman wide receiver made an impact in the return game, including a 45-yard kickoff return in the first half and a 35-yard return in the second half.

The Meh

Luke Drzewiecki. So he is human after all. A week after hitting a go-ahead 60-yard field goal in the fourth quarter against Indiana, the Gophers’ kicker missed a pair of 56-yard attempts, snapping his streak of 26 consecutive made field goals dating back to last season with New Mexico. Drzewiecki finished the game 2-of-4, with a 38-yard field goal before halftime and a 36-yarder in the fourth quarter.

The Ugly

The Minnesota secondary. What a disaster. Bruins (back-up) quarterback Ty Dieffenbach was 8-of-16 for 303 passing yards and three touchdowns, averaging 37 yards per completion. He only completed three passes in the second half, two of which went for 75-yard touchdowns on back-to-back drives. Defensive coordinator Danny Collins got flat-out outcoached by UCLA offensive coordinator Dean Kennedy in the second half. I can understand giving up one 75-yard touchdown pass. Busted coverages happen. But two? On back-to-back drives?

The first 75-yard touchdown pass comes with UCLA in 11 personnel. Two wide receivers are split out on the field side, one receiver is split out on the boundary side, and the tight end stays in to block Minnesota’s five-man rush. The outside receiver on the field side is running a post corner route (with cornerback Naiim Parrish in coverage), the inside receiver is running a deep post (with safety Kerry Brown in coverage), and the receiver on the boundary side is running what looks like a dig route to me (with cornerback John Nestor in coverage). Zack Harden is the post safety, so it’s his responsibility to protect the deep middle of the field. But he drifts too far to his left and Brown, who is expecting help over the top from Harden, gets beat deep for the easy touchdown.

The second 75-yard touchdown pass is inexcusable. Both safeties bite on the play-action fake and coming crashing down towards the box, leaving both cornerbacks in single coverage with no help over the top. Cornerback Aydan West has too much ground to cover on the field side and the wide receiver easily gets inside leverage off his break, and Dieffenbach hits him in stride for another easy touchdown.

The offense. What is there to say that hasn’t already been said? I am certain P.J. Fleck would point out that 20 points is more than the 13.4 points the Bruins’ defense was allowing per game, but this is also the fifth straight game that the Gophers have have been held to 20 points or fewer. You’re not going to win a lot of games if 20 points is your ceiling on offense. And the same issues persist, week after week. On almost every play, if it’s not one thing, it’s another. If the offensive play-call is good, the offensive line that can’t block the play effectively. If the offensive line holds up, the play design is poor and none of the receivers are open. If the receivers are open, Drake Lindsey makes a poor throw or doesn’t have the confidence to even throw the ball at all. There’s just no consistency from one play to the next. It’s a total system failure.

Injuries. Defensive tackles Riley Sunram and Jaylin Hicks were both lost to serious injuries during the game. Sunram, who has been playing through upper body injuries, went to the locker room and returned in street clothes with his arm in a sling, and Hicks left the game on a cart after his left leg had to be stabilized with an air cast. Minnesota’s five-man rotation on the interior defensive line is now likely down to a three-man rotation with Theo Randle, Naquan Crowder, and Xion Chapman.

item.title: Dolphins fan confidence remains high despite losses
item.description: Miami Dolphins fan confidence slips some in Week 9, but remains high overall.
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Dolphins lost to the New England Patriots last weekend, dropping to 1-6 and reminding everyone this is a rebuilding year. They held a 13-3 halftime lead against their AFC East rivals, but couldn’t sustain the momentum in the second half and let New England storm back for a 24-19 win.

This year is about the growth and development of the team, not necessarily about the wins and losses – but wins sure feel much better than losses.

In Week 9, the Dolphins host the Detroit Lions, a 5-2 team that is looking to return to the playoffs in 2026 after missing out last year. A physical team that gets after their opponents each and every week, Detroit serves as an example of the success a philosophy change and roster rebuild can bring.

The Lions are five years ahead of Miami on the rebuild path. The FanDuel Sportsbook oddsmakers, expect Detroit to use that advantage to come away with the win on Sunday. The Lions are a 6.5-point favorite for the game.

Dolphins fan confidence

Despite the losses mounting, Dolphins fans seem to see the course laid out by general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and head coach Jeff Hafley. Both in their first year in the roles, they have been deliberate in how they reset the Dolphins’ salary cap, roster, and play style. They have the players believing in them, and the fans seem to also trust them.

Each week, we ask you to weigh in on how you are feeling about the direction of the Dolphins. We then track the results of our SB Nation Reacts surveys to see how the fan base is feeling about the team, and how it changes over the course of the season. This year, the fans have consistently demonstrated their trust for the new management team and in the direction of the franchise.

That doesn’t mean the losses don’t affect fans’ feelings. Heading into last week, 97 percent of fans thought Miami was headed in the right direction, nearing an all-time high after the team’s win over the New York Jets. After the loss to the New England Patriots in Week 8, and as they prepare to face the Detroit Lions in Week 9, fan confidence dropped somewhat, but support for the team remains overwhelming.

After 97 percent of respondents said they felt positive about the Dolphins’ direction in Week 8, that number slipped to 86 percent in Week 9.

How will this weekend’s game impact the results in Week 10?

item.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em Sit 'Em: Week 9 lineup advice from Justin Boone
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Justin Boone shares his top sits and starts for Week 9.
item.content:encoded:
Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench. 

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 9 rankings. 

Starts

Dak Prescott, QB, Cowboys

at Colts

It's almost surprising that Prescott is the QB11 in fantasy points per game this year, considering he went a month without a multi-touchdown game at one point. Fortunately, he's found the end zone at least twice in each of the past two weeks. 

Now, Prescott faces a Colts team that's circling the drain before a likely selloff at the trade deadline. In its first game after dealing Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, Indy was dismantled 42-7 by the Jaguars. The Cowboys are 4.5-point favorites on the road with the third-highest implied point total on the week. 

Though Dak hasn't been the most reliable fantasy option this season, you can start him confidently as a top-five QB versus the Colts. 

Other QBs to start:

  • Malik Willis vs. Lions – With the Dolphins' young receiving corps getting healthy, Willis has been heating up lately as a solid fantasy streamer who offers a high floor and high ceiling. This is setting up to be a potential ceiling game for him, against a Detroit defense giving up the most fantasy points to QBs, including multiple TDs in every outing.  

  • C.J. Stroud at Chargers – Stroud has quietly had a very solid season and, with the Texans' struggles in the run game, you can expect the team to continue relying on his arm. The 25-year-old is tied for the fifth most fantasy points among quarterbacks over the last five weeks. Coming off the bye, Stroud should get a boost from Marvin Harrison Jr. getting more comfortable in the offense and Tank Dell seeing a rise in snaps. 

Chase Brown, RB, Bengals

at Falcons

Brown only finished as the RB20 in a great matchup with the Titans last week, but that would have been a top-12 fantasy back if his 20-yard touchdown catch wasn't nullified by a penalty. 

The good news is that Brown continues to dominate the Bengals backfield, playing almost 70% of the snaps last week and turning them into 20 touches, 101 scrimmage yards and eight catches. 

He also gets another positive matchup with the Falcons defense that's the fourth-easiest matchup for fantasy running backs. Atlanta has allowed seven touchdowns to RBs over its last three games and just got decimated for over 300 rushing yards by the Buccaneers backs in Week 8. 

I know it's been frustrating at times having Brown in your lineup; just don't give up now. Bigger days are within reach. If you are planning to sell him, you'll want to wait until after this game to get the most value. 

Other RBs to start:

  • Jonah Coleman at Panthers – Coleman returned from IR and immediately took control of the Broncos backfield, playing 58% of the snaps over the last two weeks and racking up 173 scrimmage yards, six receptions and a touchdown. Now, he gets a Panthers defense that's permitting the second-most fantasy points to his position. The rookie is a top-15 fantasy RB option this week. 

  • Blake Corum at Commanders – Over the last month, the Rams offense has leaned on their backfield more with Davante Adams hitting IR. That resulted in both backs averaging top-15 fantasy stats, with Corum at RB13 and Kyren Williams at RB15. Don't be misled; Williams is still the lead back and Corum hasn't played over 50% of the snaps in any game. However, he's getting plenty of opportunity, which should continue as 5.5-point favorites over the Commanders. 

  • Tyler Allgeier at Seahawks – While I hate the matchup, it's impossible to argue with the setup for Allgeier. Jeremiyah Love is on IR and Bam Knight is in concussion protocol. That leaves Allgeier as the last man standing in Arizona's RB room. Though you can't expect another 191-yard, five-catch, two-touchdown performance (because he's not playing the Cowboys defense), Allgeier can still be started as a volume-based, low-end RB2.

Justin Jefferson, WR, Vikings

vs. Bills

Jefferson isn't a name that makes it to the Start section very often because he's such a talented player that fantasy managers don't need a reminder. However, given the state of the quarterback play in Minnesota, starting Jefferson wasn't as obvious as it had been in the past. 

The veteran wideout has been held to receiving-yard totals of 55, 32, 44 and 33 in four of his last five outings and Kyler Murray wasn't finding his rhythm in Kevin O'Connell's scheme. 

Murray's new hamstring injury gave the coaching staff a chance to make a change and they jumped on it, naming Carson Wentz the starter for Monday's matchup with the Bills. With Buffalo's defense still being a work in progress, Wentz and company should be able to get the Vikings' passing game back on track. 

That's great news for Jefferson, who has averaged 6.4 receptions and 89.1 receiving yards during the seven games where Wentz has played at least 80% of the snaps over the last two seasons. That includes an 8-92-2 stat line from the opener this year. 

This move pushed Jefferson back into the top-10 fantasy WRs and in the conversation for a spot in the top-five for as long as Wentz is under center. 

Other WRs to start:

  • George Pickens at Colts – Pickens has been playing through shoulder and hamstring injuries the last couple of weeks and his playing time has taken a slight hit because of it. Jerry Jones was very clear this week that he believes Pickens needs to be getting the ball more, so this could be the rare squeaky wheel game initiated by the owner. As it stands, Pickens is still 14th in receiving yards among wideouts, but that ranking could rise thanks to a matchup with the Colts. 

  • Rashee Rice vs. Jets – For all the concerns about Rice before the season, he's actually performed well in every outing. Rice has at least 83 yards or a touchdown in all four of his healthy appearances, including a 7-53-1 stat line in his first game back last week, despite only playing 56% of the snaps. That number should rise in a favorable spot against a Jets defense that plays a lot of single-high coverage, which Rice excels against. 

  • Rome Odunze vs. Buccaneers – Odunze is 20th in receiving yards, but 53rd in fantasy points scored among wideouts. The discrepancy exists due to a lack of touchdowns, with Odunze not finding the end zone yet this season. Fortunately, the offense has been regaining its form with Caleb Williams back and Odunze has posted two of his best outings this season in recent weeks, with 69 yards against the Patriots and 87 yards versus the Seahawks. Next up is a Bucs defense that's allowed five different WRs to top 85 yards in the last month. 

Sam LaPorta, TE, Lions

at Dolphins

Through the first five weeks, LaPorta was a top-five fantasy tight end against one of the easier schedules at his position. Then came a bye, followed by back-to-back matchups against the two toughest defenses against his position: the Packers and Vikings. 

That led conspiracy theorists to speculate that the team was punishing LaPorta for his comments about being frustrated with contract extension talks with the organization. I'm guessing the degree of difficulty being turned up on him had more to do with it. 

Thankfully, a softer matchup has arrived with the Dolphins defense giving up the third-most fantasy points to tight ends. The Lions are also tied for the fourth-highest implied point total on the slate. This all points to a bounce-back week for LaPorta, which is why he's back in my top five. 

Other TEs to start:

  • Kyle Pitts Sr. vs. Bengals – After three straight top-12 TE finishes, Pitts finally came back down to earth with just two catches for six yards in a rainy loss to the Bucs last week. Now, he suits up for a potential shootout in Spain against a Bengals defense that's the ninth-most generous unit to tight ends. 

  • Mike Gesicki at Falcons – You can also start the other tight end in that game, with Gesicki having a great chance to extend his touchdown streak versus Atlanta. The veteran has scored a touchdown in six of his seven outings and currently sits as the TE6 in fantasy points per game. You could do worse than streaming him in a game that has the highest projected point total at 52.5. 

Sits

Bryce Young, QB, Panthers

vs. Broncos

It seems like the distant past now, but Young was the QB4 overall in fantasy points per game through the first six weeks, in part thanks to an easy early-season schedule. Life comes at you fast, though and a slew of injuries on the offensive line have completely changed the outlook for this offense. It doesn't help that their last two opponents have been much tougher, the Buccaneers and Packers, leading to a test that Young ultimately failed. 

Coming off his two lowest fantasy outputs of the season, Young now has another difficult challenge ahead with the Broncos defense that got back Patrick Surtain II last week. There will be better days ahead, including the Saints matchup in Week 10, but for now, Young needs to head to your bench. 

Other QBs to sit:

  • Geno Smith at Chiefs – Kansas City's defense is allowing the sixth-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks and tends to be even more stout at home. Meanwhile, the Jets will be without their top receiver Garrett Wilson, who is in concussion protocol. This isn't the spot to play Smith. 

  • Baker Mayfield at Bears – At some point, Mayfield will begin throwing again and this could be the week, since he's facing a high-scoring Bears offense. But forgive me if I'm not interested in starting a quarterback who hasn't topped 13 fantasy points in a game this season and has only attempted 14 passes over the last two weeks. 

Rachaad White, RB, Commanders

vs. Rams

White came through in Week 8 thanks to a touchdown, but his usage (13 touches, 47% snap share) was disappointing given the matchup with the Eagles and the fact that Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on IR. 

The situation isn't getting better this week against a Rams defense that's his toughest opponent yet. Not only are they allowing the seventh-fewest fantasy points to running backs, but Myles Garrett is expected back for the game. 

This all points to a risky setup for White, who will likely need another touchdown to save his fantasy day again. 

Other RBs to sit:

  • Zach Charbonnet vs. Cardinals – The Seahawks are 8.5-point favorites, so the possibility of a goal-line carry is always there. However, it's tough to get overly excited about Charbonnet, who managed just 29 yards on nine touches while playing 37% of the snaps in his season debut. Rookie Jadarian Price displayed far more juice during the game and should earn more touches moving forward, while Charbonnet remains in a supporting role. 

  • Omarion Hampton vs. Texans – Coming off the bye, Hampton played a season-low 29.5% of the snaps. The sophomore back has only topped 56 scrimmage yards once this season. Like most of the running backs in this section, he's purely a TD-or-bust RB3. 

  • Jordan Mason vs. Bills – Mason returned to the lineup in Week 7 with a 64% snap share and 15 carries for 68 yards. Unfortunately, just one week later, those numbers dropped to 28% of the snaps and just eight carries for 20 yards. While the matchup with the Bills is a positive one, it's hard to trust Mason until we see more from him and the Vikings offense as a whole. 

Michael Wilson, WR, Cardinals

at Seahawks

Wilson finally rediscovered his ceiling with an eight-catch, 111-yard, one-touchdown performance, but it took a very friendly matchup with the Cowboys to get there. 

Wilson also accomplished the feat while playing through two broken ribs, something that will continue to be a challenge this week. 

It's also worth remembering that Wilson was held to 55 yards or less in three straight games before that springboard encounter with Dallas. The Seahawks defense, which is giving up the fewest fantasy points to wideouts, won't be the same kind of pushover. That makes Wilson a volatile WR3. 

Other WRs to sit:

  • Jalen Coker vs. Broncos – The issues on the offensive line and the difficult matchup with the Broncos defense are more than enough reason to avoid Coker this week. He's only managed three catches over his last two outings. 

  • Chris Godwin Jr. at Bears – Godwin hasn't topped 50 receiving yards in a game this season and hasn't reached 40 yards in his last six appearances. Injuries have simply sapped his effectiveness, and given his age, it's likely his best days are behind him.  

  • Xavier Worthy vs. Jets – Worthy has been held to 25 yards or less in five of his seven games this season. He's also only found the end zone once all year, making him a very shaky flex option at best. 

Dalton Kincaid, TE, Bills

at Vikings

Kincaid's best performances have coincided with DJ Moore being in the lineup, which gives you hope that he can get back to being a top-10 fantasy tight end the rest of the way. Unfortunately, this week's matchup is with the Vikings defense, which is the biggest threat to tight ends by far this season. 

Minnesota is allowing just 5.5 fantasy points per game, with the second-place Packers coming in at 7.0 fppg. The Vikings also haven't allowed a touchdown to a tight end and we've yet to see them give up more than 65 yards to a player at the position. Even if you look back to last year, Brian Flores' crew was the eighth-worst opponent for tight ends. If Kincaid comes through this week, it will be an outlier based on what we've seen from this defense in 2026. 

Other TEs to sit:

  • Chig Okonkwo vs. Rams – After back-to-back 60-plus-yard games, Okonkwo managed just two catches for 32 yards in a tougher matchup with the Eagles last week. The Rams are the seventh most difficult opponent for fantasy tight ends, so I wouldn't get my hopes up here. 

  • Tyler Higbee at Commanders – Higbee has been held to 22 yards, 14 yards and 14 yards over his last three outings.

item.description: Rise and shine, NFL fans! The Bengals and Falcons play in Madrid at 6:30 am PT, before Seahawks fans key in on Rams at Commanders at 10 am. Let’s chat!
item.content:encoded:
We’ve got ourselves another early morning NFL game to look forward to, Seattle Seahawks fans! It’s the Cincinnati Bengals and the Atlanta Falcons at the Santiago Bernabeu, aka the home of Real Madrid in Madrid, Spain. It won’t be Kylian Mbappe rampaging through a defense; it’ll be Bijan Robinson trying to get on track against the Bengals defense. It’s a battle of 5-3 teams at Gillette Stadium in Week 9. Trying to win a second straight game and take some momentum into their trip to Germany next week, the New England Patriots will play hosts to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.

The Packers are a good football team and one of the most challenging opponents Mike Vrabel’s team will have faced so far this season. That said, according to FanDuel Sportsbook, the Patriots are still regarded as three-point favorites at home. Will they live up to that status? Or will the Packers manage to steal a victory? Let’s find out fwhat Pats Pulpit’s staff and community think.

Despite their personnel questions — something Green Bay is also dealing with — the Patriots do match up well with the visitors on both sides of the ball. item.title: Bengals vs. Falcons: NFL Week 9 in Madrid discussion
item.description: The NFL’s next European game of the season will kick-off in Madrid, Spain in Week 9.
item.content:encoded:
The Cincinnati Bengals (5-2) and the Atlanta Falcons (3-5) are set to face off on Sunday morning in Madrid for the next European game of the 2026 NFL season.

The Bengals lead the all-time series between these teams, 10-5, and have won their most-recent three meetings. They last faced off back in 2022, when the Bengals got a big win home in Cincinnati, 35-17.

One of the storylines in this matchup is former Eagles quarterback Andy Dalton, sitting at the No. 3 QB for the Falcons against the Bengals, which is the team that drafted him in 2011. Dalton chose to sign with Atlanta instead of returning the Eagles practice squad when they released him a few weeks ago, and now he’s facing another former team in Spain.

Dalton is also just the last Philly alumni signed with the Falcons, joining SAF Sydney Brown, WR Jahan Dotson, CB Robert Longerbeam, EDGE Za’Darius Smith, and WR Olamide Zaccheaus. The only former Eagles players for the Bengals are LB Oren Burks and QB2 Joe Flacco.

item.title: James Pearce Jr. is active for the Falcons
item.description: The eight-game suspension of Falcons defensive end James Pearce Jr. has ended.
item.content:encoded:
The eight-game suspension of Falcons defensive end James Pearce Jr. has ended. His second NFL season officially starts on Sunday in Madrid.

Pearce is active for the Week 9 game against the Bengals.

Pearce will play despite back tightness that made him a limited participant in Friday's practice.

The inactives for the Falcons on Sunday include quarterback Andy Dalton (emergency QB), quarterback Jack Strand, receiver Zachariah Branch, cornerback Billy Bowman Jr., cornerback Robert Longerbeam, and defensive end Drake Jackson.

Bowman, who missed the last two games with a hamstring, was considered to be healthy and ready to return.

Also out are running back Brian Robinson Jr. and defensive end Samson Ekuban. Both were placed on injured reserve recently, taking them off the 53-man roster.

A first-round pick in 2025, Pearce had 10.5 sacks as a rookie, and he finished third in the NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year voting. Felony charges filed after he repeatedly rammed his ex-girlfriend's car and resisted arrest triggered the eight-game suspension.
